blocks.text: Barkpark Tasks mobile · preparation paper 1 of 5 · lane identity-cascade · 2026-07-23

content.value: Cloud is the front door: identity, server selection, and the auto-select cascade

Barkpark Tasks — the mobile hybrid of the chat app and the task app — needs a spine before any pixel: Barkpark Cloud login → select server → workspace → project → dataset, auto-selecting the only option at every level and remembering the last. This paper establishes ground truth for that spine. The verdict: every piece already exists and is live-proven except one joint — nothing today turns a Cloud identity into a portable, per-user data-plane token that a plain team member can hold. The epic builds that one hinge; the rest of the cascade is a client-side port of proven CLI logic.

items.label: cascade levels already have live, membership-scoped list endpoints — none is missing
paths today hand a plain team MEMBER a portable data-plane bearer token — the epic's one hard build
gated Cloud routes accept a PAT; the rest demand a live session — the phone's credential is the 30-day session
the smallest token that reads tasks + papers + search AND drives chat — write is only needed to CREATE
items.value: [read,chat]

content.value: One hinge, then a port

The v1 login-to-first-screen: the phone drives the already-shipped RFC-8628 device flow against Cloud (system browser to /activate, poll every 5 s, session minted AT POLL so the token never touches the browser), lands a 30-day Cloud session in Keychain/Keystore, enumerates the fleet with GET /v1/barkparks?scope=all (auto-select if exactly one, cache the last), then exchanges the Cloud session for a per-server APP TOKEN through two NEW endpoints — the only genuinely new machinery in this lane — and walks the instance cascade GET /api/workspaces → projects → datasets, auto-selecting on count==1 and remembering the last location client-side. Interview constraint honored: the app is EXCLUSIVE to Barkpark Cloud at the start — Cloud auth is the identity layer, and 'any Barkpark server' is reached through Cloud's registry (adopted self-hosted boxes included), with manual token paste as the universal escape hatch exactly as the CLI does it.

blocks.caption: Proposed v1 login-to-first-screen. Steps 1-4 and 7-8 are shipped machinery; only the two starred endpoints are new. The phone is the REQUESTING device (start + poll only); the browser is the approver.

content.value: Cloud POST /v1/barkparks/:id/app-token — user-session-authed, team-scoped, reachable by ANY team member; server-side it uses the instance admin token stored in the registry, exactly the proven studio-link pattern (cloud router.ex:1886-1935) — the admin token never travels to the phone. It calls a NEW instance endpoint, POST /v1/auth/app-tokens (admin-gated), which JIT-provisions the Cloud user by email via Sso.find_or_create_user (sso.ex:69-80), grants a MEMBER membership through Tenancy.Auth.create_membership/4 — the codebase's single Membership insertion point (tenancy/auth.ex:84-101) — and mints a per-user, workspace-bound api_token with an app permission set and expires_at. Everything the mint needs already exists: api_tokens carry expires_at + revoked_at enforced in the verify WHERE (auth.ex:44-53), and RequireChatAccess already honors a workspace token whose permissions include chat (require_chat_access.ex:55-58). Lifetime and revocation are policy choices, not schema work.

blocks.title: The one hinge: a two-endpoint token exchange

blocks.value:
# Cloud (control plane) — NEW
POST /v1/barkparks/:id/app-token          auth: user SESSION (any team member; PAT rejected)
  body: { workspace: <slug|omit=Default>, permissions?: subset }
  -> server-side, with stored admin token: POST <instance>/v1/auth/app-tokens
  <- 201 { token: "bp_...", workspace_id, permissions, expires_at }   # plaintext once
  <- 404 no_admin_token — instance never stored one -> manual-paste fallback

# Instance (data plane) — NEW
POST /v1/auth/app-tokens                   auth: admin api_token (Cloud-held, server-side only)
  body: { email, workspace, permissions: ["read","write","chat"], expires_in_days }
  1. Sso.find_or_create_user(email)        # idempotent, pre-confirmed (sso.ex:69-80)
  2. create_membership(ws, user, "member", "user")   # constraint-idempotent
  3. Auth mint: kind=api, workspace_id=ws, expires_at  # NOT the chat mint (D48 stays hardcoded)

# Refresh story (no new machinery): on 401, silently re-mint through the
# still-valid 30-day Cloud session; when THAT dies, full device-flow re-login.

content.value: The auto-select + last-location behavior the wish describes is not an invention — it is a port. The CLI already auto-connects a single-Barkpark fleet with no prompt (setup_cloud_login.go:142-146, ratified as decision 19's n==1 fast path in the bp-login-ux charter) and already persists Server/Workspace/Project/Dataset plus a most-recent-first KnownServers list (config.go:29-58). The mobile client replicates that state machine over its own secure store. One server-side courtesy is worth adding while we are here: projects already sort the canonical default-slug project first (tenancy.ex:858-869) but datasets have no production-first equivalent (tenancy.ex:1045-1047) — a two-line ordering fix that makes every consumer's take-the-first behavior correct.

head: Design fork
Rival
Verdict
rows: Where the exchange lives
Cloud proxy using the stored admin token vs a Cloud-signed assertion the instance verifies directly
PROXY for v1 — the studio-link pattern is proven live and needs no new trust root. The assertion design is the only path for never-adopted servers; keep it as the named v2 successor, not v1 scope.
Machine-API credential
Mint per-user api_tokens vs teach RequireToken to accept instance user sessions
MINT — RequireToken is deliberately api_token-only (require_token.ex:10-16); widening it has huge blast radius and breaks the ratified api_token/user-session separation.
Cloud PAT as the phone's credential
PAT (long-lived, scoped) vs 30-day session

SESSION — PATs are structurally invisible to 68 of 74 gated Cloud routes: require_user only queries context=='session' rows (accounts.ex:548-570), so scope=all, credentials and studio-link all 401 a PAT.
Role granted at JIT mint
MEMBER (SSO/SCIM precedent) vs OWNER (studio-link precedent)

MEMBER — studio-link's Default-workspace OWNER grant is explicitly justified by the instance-admin-token trust chain for a browser session (session_controller.ex:95-98); copying that generosity into portable tokens crosses a line the studio-link authors never accepted. SSO grants member (sso.ex:15), SCIM grants member (scim.ex:23).
Permission set on the app token
[read,chat] minimal vs [read,write,chat] sweet spot

[read,write,chat] RECOMMENDED — tasks routes check no permission at all and claim/close/stamp are workflow ops, but CREATING a task rides /v1/data/mutate which requires write (router.ex:1677-1680). A tasks app that cannot file a task is not the sweet spot. Ship [read,chat] only if the product lane picks extreme minimalism.
Token topology
One token per (user, server, workspace), mint-on-switch vs one per (user, server)

PER-WORKSPACE, mint-on-switch, cached per (server, workspace) — chat's owner_workspace_id = token.workspace_id forces the binding; the rival needs a chat-scope relaxation nobody has designed. Genuinely open on sprawl tolerance — see open questions.

content.value: Login plumbing, as shipped

Three facts organize everything. First: the Cloud device flow is mobile-ready as-is — start/poll are unauthenticated but rate-limited, TTL 600 s, interval 5 s, and the session is minted at poll time after atomically consuming the approved row (device_auth.ex:29-43, 219-257), byte-identical to password login. Second: the machine API on every instance accepts ONLY api_tokens — RequireToken verifies Bearer via Auth.verify_token (kind==api, revoked_at NULL, expires_at NULL-or-future) and every tasks route rides that pipeline (tasks.ex:432-461; router/plugins.ex:47); instance user sessions exist but drive only /v1/auth/* and Studio. Third: today's only Cloud-to-instance credential paths dead-end for a plain member — the diagram below is the whole map.

blocks.caption: Today's plumbing. Solid arrows work; dashed arrows are the dead ends that make the token exchange mandatory. No path reaches the machine API for a plain team member.

content.value: Behind Caddy in prod, conn.remote_ip resolves to the loopback/docker-bridge address for every client, so the start:<ip> device-auth bucket collapses to ONE GLOBAL 10-per-60 s budget for all Cloud device-login starts fleet-wide (tracked in cch-w1-peer-ip-pin, open). A widely-installed mobile app could exhaust it by itself and starve every CLI login too. Fixing peer-IP resolution is a hard prerequisite of any wide mobile rollout — it belongs in the epic's auth workstream, not as a hope.

items.value: What a plain team member on a phone cannot obtain today:

no instance admin token (403), no bootstrap token (403), no chat token (needs instance owner/admin), no app-grade token from TokenController (422 by contract), and the one thing a member CAN mint — a studio-link — lands as a browser cookie no HTTP client can persist or replay.
What a member CAN do today:
device-login, list the all-teams fleet, open Studio in a WebView via studio-link, and read any published paper anonymously — /papers/:slug requires no auth at all (bulldocs.ex:183-184).

content.value: Two consequences. First: below Cloud, the auto-select cascade is entirely client-side — the app counts list length itself and keeps its own most-recent-used memory at every level, exactly as the CLI config does. Second, a wrinkle this lane flags but shares with the tasks lane: the three product surfaces land at DIFFERENT cascade depths. Chat is workspace-scoped (token-bound), tasks are flat-mounted at host root /v1/tasks — effectively Default-workspace-shaped, with no /w/:ws scoped mirror (tasks.ex:432-461) — and papers/data are dataset-scoped. The wish's five-level cascade is therefore a NAVIGATION spine, not a uniform authorization spine; the epic must decide per-tab what the selected dataset actually scopes, and whether tasks stay flat for v1. Routing note for the router.ex reader: the /api/workspaces registration lives at router.ex:2449-2465 — the ~2392-2410 range cited in earlier notes is media routes.
Eight findings that bend the design

items.value: The minimal token is [read,chat], not [read,write,chat].

Every /v1/tasks* route runs bare RequireToken — any valid token passes, no permission check; claim/close/stamp are workflow ops by explicit moduledoc (tasks.ex:417-421). Document reads need read; chat needs chat+workspace. Write guards exactly one thing the app wants: creating tasks/docs via /v1/data/mutate.
Paper editing structurally exceeds every non-admin token.

All three Bulldocs mutation routes (ingest, apply_op, propose) ride the :ingest pipeline — shared ingest secret or ADMIN token only, no write/chat path exists (require_ingest_token.ex:24-50; bulldocs.ex:202-207). The wish's eventual-editing ambition silently contradicts this lane's token design unless the epic declares a per-user ops seam. This is a crown-level ruling, named openly here rather than papered over.
PATs are structurally invisible, not merely rejected.

require_user only ever queries context=='session' rows — a PAT cannot satisfy it in principle (accounts.ex:548-570). The client.go comment about team-scoped PATs is functionally right, mechanistically imprecise. Only 6 of 74 gated Cloud routes accept a PAT at all.
/papers/barkpark-cloud-goal does not exist.

The auth-tunnel / five-credential-gates framing this lane was chartered to cite is session-memory folklore — bp paper view 404s and no paper-type document carries it. The actual ratified prior art is .claude/workflows/bp-login-ux-charter.md: 25 decisions, waves 1-3 merged, including the n==1 fleet fast path and decision 15's stored-admin-token trust posture. The token exchange extends that charter; it does not contradict it.
There is no attach-later for admin tokens.

admin_token_encrypted is writable through exactly one changeset (health_changeset, barkpark.ex:456-471) with exactly two worker-gated one-shot callers (adopt, provision-success). No route, CLI verb, or changeset attaches or rotates it afterwards — an instance adopted without --admin-token is permanently stuck at no_admin_token, fixable only by destructive re-adoption.
The JIT machinery is small, shared, and precedented.

Sso.find_or_create_user is idempotent (repeat call = pure read) and already serves SAML and the Cloud ticket flow; create_membership/4 is the codebase's single Membership insertion point, constraint-idempotent. Four live precedents do find-or-create + grant; the role split is clean: browser-console flows grant OWNER, directory/SSO flows grant MEMBER.
Reading a published paper needs no token at all.
/papers/:slug is auth: :public_root — fully anonymous (bulldocs.ex:183-184). The papers tab can render before the token exchange completes; only search/query surfaces need read.
Expiry and revocation are already schema-complete.

Auth.verify_token enforces kind==api AND revoked_at NULL AND expires_at NULL-or-future in the WHERE clause (auth.ex:44-53). Cloud sessions are 30 d with per-device revocation. The whole lifetime/refresh question is policy, not plumbing.

content.value: The auth workstream is smaller than feared and sharper than hoped: two endpoints, one role decision, one rate-limit fix — and one honest contradiction to rule on before anyone promises paper editing.

content.value: Honest residue

(1) The global device-start bucket: 10 starts/60 s shared fleet-wide in prod — a popular app DoSes its own login and everyone else's (cch-w1-peer-ip-pin). (2) Token sprawl: per-workspace minting multiplies tokens per user; without a list/revoke surface the revocation story degrades to revoke-the-Cloud-session. (3) Role creep: copying studio-link's OWNER grant into tokens would silently hand every team member owner authority on instances — the mint must grant member. (4) Version skew: old or self-hosted instances lack the new mint endpoint — the app needs capability detection and the manual-paste fallback everywhere. (5) No refresh machinery: the silent re-mint story depends on Cloud reachability at 401 time; offline-expiry UX needs design. (6) find_or_create_user has a get-then-insert race under concurrent first logins. (7) The paper-editing contradiction: an app token can NEVER edit papers under today's pipelines — promising editing without the new seam would ship a lie.

items.value: Token topology:
per (user, server, workspace) with mint-on-switch (recommended; chat forces workspace binding) vs per (user, server) with a chat-scope relaxation. How much sprawl is acceptable?
Permission set:
[read,write,chat] (recommended sweet spot — write is task creation) vs [read,chat] minimalism. Couples to the product lane's chosen shape.
Lifetime policy:
expiring app tokens (7-30 d) with silent re-mint vs non-expiring CLI-style. Is re-mint-through-the-session an acceptable refresh story, or does the epic build real refresh tokens?
Exchange architecture beyond v1:
keep the Cloud proxy only, or also design the Cloud-signed assertion path that works for instances that never stored an admin token?
Scope of any Barkpark server in v1:
Cloud-registered + manual paste (CLI precedent) — or defer un-adopted self-hosted servers entirely?
The attach/rotate verb:
build bp cloud instance credentials set/rotate in this epic (fixes the permanently-stuck no_admin_token class) or accept destructive re-adoption?
The paper-editing seam:
declare a per-user ops route/permission in-epic, or ship v1 read-only papers and defer? Joint ruling with the tasks-papers lane — the capstone must decide once.
Tasks tenancy depth:
tasks are flat-mounted at host root today — does the mobile cascade force workspace-scoped task routes, or does v1 accept flat? Flagged here; the tasks lane owns it.

body_html:
Barkpark Tasks mobile · preparation paper 1 of 5 · lane identity-cascade · 2026-07-23

Cloud is the front door: identity, server selection, and the auto-select cascade

Barkpark Tasks — the mobile hybrid of the chat app and the task app — needs a spine before any pixel: Barkpark Cloud login → select server → workspace → project → dataset, auto-selecting the only option at every level and remembering the last. This paper establishes ground truth for that spine. The verdict: every piece already exists and is live-proven except one joint — nothing today turns a Cloud identity into a portable, per-user data-plane token that a plain team member can hold. The epic builds that one hinge; the rest of the cascade is a client-side port of proven CLI logic.

Device-flow client contract · Credential-flow map · Cascade endpoint inventory · The token exchange · Today vs epic-must-build · Files · risks · coverage

4/4
cascade levels already have live, membership-scoped list endpoints — none is missing
0
paths today hand a plain team MEMBER a portable data-plane bearer token — the epic's one hard build
6/74
gated Cloud routes accept a PAT; the rest demand a live session — the phone's credential is the 30-day session
[read,chat]
the smallest token that reads tasks + papers + search AND drives chat — write is only needed to CREATE
§
  1. What we will create
  2. How the system works today
  3. The cascade, level by level
  4. What we learned
  5. Today vs epic-must-build
  6. Files likely to change
  7. Risks and open questions
  8. Coverage appendix

01 · What we will create

One hinge, then a port

The v1 login-to-first-screen: the phone drives the already-shipped RFC-8628 device flow against Cloud (system browser to /activate, poll every 5 s, session minted AT POLL so the token never touches the browser), lands a 30-day Cloud session in Keychain/Keystore, enumerates the fleet with GET /v1/barkparks?scope=all (auto-select if exactly one, cache the last), then exchanges the Cloud session for a per-server APP TOKEN through two NEW endpoints — the only genuinely new machinery in this lane — and walks the instance cascade GET /api/workspaces → projects → datasets, auto-selecting on count==1 and remembering the last location client-side. Interview constraint honored: the app is EXCLUSIVE to Barkpark Cloud at the start — Cloud auth is the identity layer, and 'any Barkpark server' is reached through Cloud's registry (adopted self-hosted boxes included), with manual token paste as the universal escape hatch exactly as the CLI does it.

The one hinge: a two-endpoint token exchange Cloud POST /v1/barkparks/:id/app-token — user-session-authed, team-scoped, reachable by ANY team member; server-side it uses the instance admin token stored in the registry, exactly the proven studio-link pattern (cloud router.ex:1886-1935) — the admin token never travels to the phone. It calls a NEW instance endpoint, POST /v1/auth/app-tokens (admin-gated), which JIT-provisions the Cloud user by email via Sso.find_or_create_user (sso.ex:69-80), grants a MEMBER membership through Tenancy.Auth.create_membership/4 — the codebase's single Membership insertion point (tenancy/auth.ex:84-101) — and mints a per-user, workspace-bound api_token with an app permission set and expires_at. Everything the mint needs already exists: api_tokens carry expires_at + revoked_at enforced in the verify WHERE (auth.ex:44-53), and RequireChatAccess already honors a workspace token whose permissions include chat (require_chat_access.ex:55-58). Lifetime and revocation are policy choices, not schema work.
# Cloud (control plane) — NEW
POST /v1/barkparks/:id/app-token          auth: user SESSION (any team member; PAT rejected)
  body: { workspace: <slug|omit=Default>, permissions?: subset }
  -> server-side, with stored admin token: POST <instance>/v1/auth/app-tokens
  <- 201 { token: "bp_...", workspace_id, permissions, expires_at }   # plaintext once
  <- 404 no_admin_token — instance never stored one -> manual-paste fallback

# Instance (data plane) — NEW
POST /v1/auth/app-tokens                   auth: admin api_token (Cloud-held, server-side only)
  body: { email, workspace, permissions: ["read","write","chat"], expires_in_days }
  1. Sso.find_or_create_user(email)        # idempotent, pre-confirmed (sso.ex:69-80)
  2. create_membership(ws, user, "member", "user")   # constraint-idempotent
  3. Auth mint: kind=api, workspace_id=ws, expires_at  # NOT the chat mint (D48 stays hardcoded)

# Refresh story (no new machinery): on 401, silently re-mint through the
# still-valid 30-day Cloud session; when THAT dies, full device-flow re-login.

The auto-select + last-location behavior the wish describes is not an invention — it is a port. The CLI already auto-connects a single-Barkpark fleet with no prompt (setup_cloud_login.go:142-146, ratified as decision 19's n==1 fast path in the bp-login-ux charter) and already persists Server/Workspace/Project/Dataset plus a most-recent-first KnownServers list (config.go:29-58). The mobile client replicates that state machine over its own secure store. One server-side courtesy is worth adding while we are here: projects already sort the canonical default-slug project first (tenancy.ex:858-869) but datasets have no production-first equivalent (tenancy.ex:1045-1047) — a two-line ordering fix that makes every consumer's take-the-first behavior correct.

Design forkRivalVerdict
Where the exchange livesCloud proxy using the stored admin token vs a Cloud-signed assertion the instance verifies directlyPROXY for v1 — the studio-link pattern is proven live and needs no new trust root. The assertion design is the only path for never-adopted servers; keep it as the named v2 successor, not v1 scope.
Machine-API credentialMint per-user api_tokens vs teach RequireToken to accept instance user sessionsMINT — RequireToken is deliberately api_token-only (require_token.ex:10-16); widening it has huge blast radius and breaks the ratified api_token/user-session separation.
Cloud PAT as the phone's credentialPAT (long-lived, scoped) vs 30-day sessionSESSION — PATs are structurally invisible to 68 of 74 gated Cloud routes: require_user only queries context=='session' rows (accounts.ex:548-570), so scope=all, credentials and studio-link all 401 a PAT.
Role granted at JIT mintMEMBER (SSO/SCIM precedent) vs OWNER (studio-link precedent)MEMBER — studio-link's Default-workspace OWNER grant is explicitly justified by the instance-admin-token trust chain for a browser session (session_controller.ex:95-98); copying that generosity into portable tokens crosses a line the studio-link authors never accepted. SSO grants member (sso.ex:15), SCIM grants member (scim.ex:23).
Permission set on the app token[read,chat] minimal vs [read,write,chat] sweet spot[read,write,chat] RECOMMENDED — tasks routes check no permission at all and claim/close/stamp are workflow ops, but CREATING a task rides /v1/data/mutate which requires write (router.ex:1677-1680). A tasks app that cannot file a task is not the sweet spot. Ship [read,chat] only if the product lane picks extreme minimalism.
Token topologyOne token per (user, server, workspace), mint-on-switch vs one per (user, server)PER-WORKSPACE, mint-on-switch, cached per (server, workspace) — chat's owner_workspace_id = token.workspace_id forces the binding; the rival needs a chat-scope relaxation nobody has designed. Genuinely open on sprawl tolerance — see open questions.
§

02 · How the system works today

Login plumbing, as shipped

Three facts organize everything. First: the Cloud device flow is mobile-ready as-is — start/poll are unauthenticated but rate-limited, TTL 600 s, interval 5 s, and the session is minted at poll time after atomically consuming the approved row (device_auth.ex:29-43, 219-257), byte-identical to password login. Second: the machine API on every instance accepts ONLY api_tokens — RequireToken verifies Bearer via Auth.verify_token (kind==api, revoked_at NULL, expires_at NULL-or-future) and every tasks route rides that pipeline (tasks.ex:432-461; router/plugins.ex:47); instance user sessions exist but drive only /v1/auth/* and Studio. Third: today's only Cloud-to-instance credential paths dead-end for a plain member — the diagram below is the whole map.

CallServer stateResponseRequired client action
POST /v1/auth/device/startok200 {device_code, user_code, verification_uri, interval: 5, expires_in: 600}Show code + QR, open system browser to /activate, start polling at interval
startbucket start:<ip> over 10/60 s429 {error: rate_limited}Back off with jitter — and note the bucket is effectively GLOBAL in prod (warning below)
POST /v1/auth/device/pollpending200 {status: pending}Keep polling at interval
pollapproved — row consumed atomically, mint-at-poll200 {token, team_id}Store in Keychain/Keystore, stop polling, enter the cascade
pollover 20/60 s per device_code_hash429 {error: slow_down}RFC-8628 mandate: WIDEN the poll interval, never retry at the same cadence
pollexpired · denied · replayed · unknown404 {error: expired_or_invalid}Terminal — show start over
inspect / approve / denybrowser-approver legs, Bearer-gated, shared approve:<user_id> bucket 10/60 s200 / 404 opaque / 429Not the phone's job in v1 — mobile is the REQUESTING device, like the CLI (reverse role explicitly unresolved)
Known defect the app inherits: one global start bucket Behind Caddy in prod, conn.remote_ip resolves to the loopback/docker-bridge address for every client, so the start:<ip> device-auth bucket collapses to ONE GLOBAL 10-per-60 s budget for all Cloud device-login starts fleet-wide (tracked in cch-w1-peer-ip-pin, open). A widely-installed mobile app could exhaust it by itself and starve every CLI login too. Fixing peer-IP resolution is a hard prerequisite of any wide mobile rollout — it belongs in the epic's auth workstream, not as a hope.

POST /v1/barkparks/:id/studio-link → /login/ticket/:tANY team member (require_user, router.ex:1900)single-use 60 s ticket → JIT user by email + Default-ws OWNER + a browser session COOKIE (session_controller.ex:89-146)PATTERN to copy, payload to change — proves admin-token-server-side + email handoff + JIT works; but a cookie is not a portable bearer, and OWNER is the wrong role

  • What a plain team member on a phone cannot obtain today: no instance admin token (403), no bootstrap token (403), no chat token (needs instance owner/admin), no app-grade token from TokenController (422 by contract), and the one thing a member CAN mint — a studio-link — lands as a browser cookie no HTTP client can persist or replay.
  • What a member CAN do today: device-login, list the all-teams fleet, open Studio in a WebView via studio-link, and read any published paper anonymously — /papers/:slug requires no auth at all (bulldocs.ex:183-184).
§

03 · The cascade

The cascade, level by level

LevelEndpointAuthRow shapeAuto-select hint
1 · ServerCloud GET /v1/barkparks?scope=allCloud SESSION — a PAT gets 401 (router.ex:1607-1616)RICH: id, name, slug, url, host, health_status, agent_status, last_seen_at, team{id,name,slug,role}, provider, provision/suspend state … (barkpark_json, router.ex:7482-7538)health fields usable; last_seen_at is a machine heartbeat, NOT per-user last-visited — recency memory is the client's job

4 · DatasetGET /api/workspaces/:ws/projects/:proj/datasetsapi_token; 404 no-leakBARE {id, slug, name} (workspace_controller.ex:510-527)NONE — no production-first ordering despite every project bootstrapping a production dataset (tenancy.ex:1045-1047); cheap epic add
identityCloud GET /v1/mesession OR PAT + read (router.ex:1154-1193)user{id,email,confirmed,2fa}, team, teams[{id,name,slug,role}]team list only — no barkpark/workspace data; the fleet call is always separate

Two consequences. First: below Cloud, the auto-select cascade is entirely client-side — the app counts list length itself and keeps its own most-recent-used memory at every level, exactly as the CLI config does. Second, a wrinkle this lane flags but shares with the tasks lane: the three product surfaces land at DIFFERENT cascade depths. Chat is workspace-scoped (token-bound), tasks are flat-mounted at host root /v1/tasks — effectively Default-workspace-shaped, with no /w/:ws scoped mirror (tasks.ex:432-461) — and papers/data are dataset-scoped. The wish's five-level cascade is therefore a NAVIGATION spine, not a uniform authorization spine; the epic must decide per-tab what the selected dataset actually scopes, and whether tasks stay flat for v1. Routing note for the router.ex reader: the /api/workspaces registration lives at router.ex:2449-2465 — the ~2392-2410 range cited in earlier notes is media routes.

§

04 · What we learned

Eight findings that bend the design

  1. The minimal token is [read,chat], not [read,write,chat]. Every /v1/tasks* route runs bare RequireToken — any valid token passes, no permission check; claim/close/stamp are workflow ops by explicit moduledoc (tasks.ex:417-421). Document reads need read; chat needs chat+workspace. Write guards exactly one thing the app wants: creating tasks/docs via /v1/data/mutate.
  2. Paper editing structurally exceeds every non-admin token. All three Bulldocs mutation routes (ingest, apply_op, propose) ride the :ingest pipeline — shared ingest secret or ADMIN token only, no write/chat path exists (require_ingest_token.ex:24-50; bulldocs.ex:202-207). The wish's eventual-editing ambition silently contradicts this lane's token design unless the epic declares a per-user ops seam. This is a crown-level ruling, named openly here rather than papered over.
  3. PATs are structurally invisible, not merely rejected. require_user only ever queries context=='session' rows — a PAT cannot satisfy it in principle (accounts.ex:548-570). The client.go comment about team-scoped PATs is functionally right, mechanistically imprecise. Only 6 of 74 gated Cloud routes accept a PAT at all.
  4. /papers/barkpark-cloud-goal does not exist. The auth-tunnel / five-credential-gates framing this lane was chartered to cite is session-memory folklore — bp paper view 404s and no paper-type document carries it. The actual ratified prior art is .claude/workflows/bp-login-ux-charter.md: 25 decisions, waves 1-3 merged, including the n==1 fleet fast path and decision 15's stored-admin-token trust posture. The token exchange extends that charter; it does not contradict it.
  5. There is no attach-later for admin tokens. admin_token_encrypted is writable through exactly one changeset (health_changeset, barkpark.ex:456-471) with exactly two worker-gated one-shot callers (adopt, provision-success). No route, CLI verb, or changeset attaches or rotates it afterwards — an instance adopted without --admin-token is permanently stuck at no_admin_token, fixable only by destructive re-adoption.
  6. The JIT machinery is small, shared, and precedented. Sso.find_or_create_user is idempotent (repeat call = pure read) and already serves SAML and the Cloud ticket flow; create_membership/4 is the codebase's single Membership insertion point, constraint-idempotent. Four live precedents do find-or-create + grant; the role split is clean: browser-console flows grant OWNER, directory/SSO flows grant MEMBER.
  7. Reading a published paper needs no token at all. /papers/:slug is auth: :public_root — fully anonymous (bulldocs.ex:183-184). The papers tab can render before the token exchange completes; only search/query surfaces need read.
  8. Expiry and revocation are already schema-complete. Auth.verify_token enforces kind==api AND revoked_at NULL AND expires_at NULL-or-future in the WHERE clause (auth.ex:44-53). Cloud sessions are 30 d with per-device revocation. The whole lifetime/refresh question is policy, not plumbing.

The auth workstream is smaller than feared and sharper than hoped: two endpoints, one role decision, one rate-limit fix — and one honest contradiction to rule on before anyone promises paper editing.

§

§

07 · Risks & open questions

Honest residue

Risks the epic inherits (1) The global device-start bucket: 10 starts/60 s shared fleet-wide in prod — a popular app DoSes its own login and everyone else's (cch-w1-peer-ip-pin). (2) Token sprawl: per-workspace minting multiplies tokens per user; without a list/revoke surface the revocation story degrades to revoke-the-Cloud-session. (3) Role creep: copying studio-link's OWNER grant into tokens would silently hand every team member owner authority on instances — the mint must grant member. (4) Version skew: old or self-hosted instances lack the new mint endpoint — the app needs capability detection and the manual-paste fallback everywhere. (5) No refresh machinery: the silent re-mint story depends on Cloud reachability at 401 time; offline-expiry UX needs design. (6) find_or_create_user has a get-then-insert race under concurrent first logins. (7) The paper-editing contradiction: an app token can NEVER edit papers under today's pipelines — promising editing without the new seam would ship a lie.
  1. Token topology: per (user, server, workspace) with mint-on-switch (recommended; chat forces workspace binding) vs per (user, server) with a chat-scope relaxation. How much sprawl is acceptable?
  2. Permission set: [read,write,chat] (recommended sweet spot — write is task creation) vs [read,chat] minimalism. Couples to the product lane's chosen shape.
  3. Lifetime policy: expiring app tokens (7-30 d) with silent re-mint vs non-expiring CLI-style. Is re-mint-through-the-session an acceptable refresh story, or does the epic build real refresh tokens?
  4. Exchange architecture beyond v1: keep the Cloud proxy only, or also design the Cloud-signed assertion path that works for instances that never stored an admin token?
  5. Scope of any Barkpark server in v1: Cloud-registered + manual paste (CLI precedent) — or defer un-adopted self-hosted servers entirely?
  6. The attach/rotate verb: build bp cloud instance credentials set/rotate in this epic (fixes the permanently-stuck no_admin_token class) or accept destructive re-adoption?
  7. The paper-editing seam: declare a per-user ops route/permission in-epic, or ship v1 read-only papers and defer? Joint ruling with the tasks-papers lane — the capstone must decide once.
  8. Tasks tenancy depth: tasks are flat-mounted at host root today — does the mobile cascade force workspace-scoped task routes, or does v1 accept flat? Flagged here; the tasks lane owns it.
§

description: Preparation paper for the Barkpark Tasks mobile epic, lane 1 of 5 (identity-cascade). Establishes ground truth for the app's spine — Barkpark Cloud login → server → workspace → project → dataset with 1-option auto-select and last-location memory — and proves every piece of it already ships except one joint: no path today turns a Cloud identity into a portable, per-user data-plane token a plain team member can hold. Contains the device-flow client contract (rate buckets, slow_down, mint-at-poll), the full credential-flow map with file:line anchors, the cascade endpoint inventory (all four levels exist; three are bare {id,slug,name} with no server-side auto-select hint), the TODAY vs EPIC-MUST-BUILD table, the proposed two-endpoint token exchange (Cloud session-authed proxy → instance admin-gated mint, JIT-provisioning the user as MEMBER via existing Sso/Tenancy primitives), files likely to change, and the judgment calls left open. Crown companion: barkpark-tasks-mobile-capstone.
